This game is amazing. Play it. Imagine a MOBA, but without the tedious gold/experience farming and the item-based systems that lend themselves to snowballing. Imagine a MOBA where every autoattack required aim to hit with, an entirely skill-based MOBA where, even if down to rounds to one, you can still come back by changing your own strategy and gameplay. Battlerite, the spiritual successor to Bloodline Champions, is easily the best MOBA I've ever played, indeed it is the only redeeming title in a largely stagnant genre. Great yet simple gameplay, action that gets your heart pounding, and the best thing is that even if losing badly, three rounds only take a maximum of 6 minutes. Short and sweet, and for those of us who already grind for money 8 hours a day, it represents a needed and welcome change to the MOBA genre, filled with titles where you farm for a minimum of 20 minutes before the teamfights actually start. This is the MOBA genre's saving grace.

The combat and platforming in Hollow Knight is one of the biggest components of the game and it must get it right. For the most part, it flows well though there are times where some of your abilities feel absolutely pointless. In this game, you can receive crests that upgrade your character with multiple different bonuses. These range from upped health to complete different abilities that may help you out during fights. Boss fights feel generally very fair compared to other games in this sort of style. I can only think of one that may have been a little bit much and it wasn't even that bad. My biggest complaint is only if you're using analog sticks with a controller. I found myself having a really tough time with the downwards attack, it often me frustrated when certain parts of the game required it. The platforming is very simple and shouldn't pose much difficulty even for relatively newbie platforming people.
Though this game will be more centered around the gameplay the lore can be pretty interesting. Bits and pieces of the story are scattered around the areas telling you about the past and why certain enemies act the way they do. It's one of those things that are not required at all for the experience but if you're interested in that sort of thing it's there for you.
Easily the best part of this game to me is the progression. Everything flows so well and the game falls together like a beautiful puzzle. You'll see something blocked in one area and three hours later you can go back with an upgrade and find even more of the area. These could include secret bosses, shortcuts, unlockables. Each area has a few checkpoints that truly makes you feel like you're getting through the place. Each area also has a station that you can use to fast travel to one another.
The art style and soundtrack in this game go hand in hand. It creates the atmosphere of Hollow Knight as a grim world full of losses and horror. Every soundtrack correctly suits the art style for the area and vice versa. For the most part, each area looks decently different from one another a slight downside is that the enemies styles do look pretty similar after a while though it has its reasons because of the character style choice.

If you liked Saints Row 4, you'll like Gat out of Hell. Now the first thing I should remind everyone is that it costs 20 bucks. So, don't get all your hopes up about it being a sprawling storyline with all the nooks, crannys and intricacies of SR4, because it simply isn't. Truth is, the game is rather short, and I wish it was longer. There are also no inbuilt cheats as in the other games, and no radio stations. Does that take away from the game? Maybe a bit, I do wish there was a radio station in Hell, but considering that it's supposed to be eternal damnation and torment without relief or happiness, having no radio stations makes some sense. Even though some of the cars in Hell do seem to have music coming from them.
There are also no long story quests like in the other games. Because it really amounts to a DLC expansion that has been added to and made into a stand alone game.
However, that isn't to say that the game is not fun or a blast to play, because it is. The new super powers are interesting and we finally FINALLY have true flight capabilities. Not like in SR4 which basically amounts to falling with style, in Gat out of Hell, you can truely fly around Hell for as long as you want, so long as you have the Unlimited Stamina upgrade of course. Once you have that, you can quite literally fly from one end of the map to the other and back, and not have to touch the ground. Personally, that by itself makes the game worth it for me. The flight mechanics are done extremely well and feel as natural as walking, stealing a car or shooting demons in the face.
The humor is still there, just not as much because it is short. The main mission can be completed in a few hours I'd say. Thats, of course, if you decide to just rush straight through it and not get all the power ups and all the Halo Powers. Which, if you do so, I have no idea how you expect to kick Satan's♥♥♥♥♥at the end.
Honestly, I thought it was well worth the 20 bucks I spent pre-ordering it, not to mention getting the Saints Wing Skin. Could it have been longer? Hell yes! Pun not intended. Could there have been more missions and a radio? Yes, there could, although since you won't have the excuse of being in a computer simulation and having the radio with you all the time, trying to explain or devise something similar would be difficult. Maybe the Halo can recieve radio signals? Who knows, all I know is that I enjoyed this game immensely and have no problem going back and playing for even longer.

The story is again very well written, taking place after the events of the first while introducing new characters and references to the older ones. Levels tend to be more linear and smaller but still provide great exploration. This game still is survival horror, but packs in more fight action with some horde defense modes. The design is very much like the original, with improvement in graphical quality while retaining the steampunk atmosphere. Music is also similar with good horror or action music and oldies. For those who enjoyed Bioshock, the sequel provides a great story, gameplay, and environment like the first.

I know what you're thinking: "This guy has less than 5 hous on an open world game, why is he writing a review?"
Precisely because of that.
I am only 4 hours and change into Gat out of Hell and i'm already at 72% completion. That is actual completion, not just main plotline.
This game is kind of a disappointment, unfortunately.
It's a lot of fun, don't get me wrong, flying around on demon wings and shooting demons with stake throwing shotguns straight out of Painkiller is a blast, but the game feels empty.
The characters barely speak, only Dane Vogel and the DeWinter sisters (as if we were missing those two incredibly secondary and uninteresting characters, one of which originally dies after having barely a line of her own and the other partly responsible for devouring an unreasonable amount of budget for SRIII that could've gone to better writing instead of stupid casting choices like Sasha Grey or Hulk Hogan) make a comeback from previous games, aside for the two main characters, and the lack of homies make it so that banter is impossible.
The cutscenes are hilarious and somewhat meta, and the style and setup of the plot are the usual SR fare, as in "we're having fun writing this, you'll have fun reading it", too bad in 4 hours of play I must have gotten 4 in total, and i have the feeling the next will be either the last or the one before because, spoiler, there are basically no plot missions and the next plot point i'm given, first time that I get to pick when to start a plot mission in the whoole game, is "Crash the wedding".
Each cutscene is somewhat related to a special event that starts just after it, then you're back to side activities until an arbitrary point when you've accomplished enough that the game feels like you deserve another slice of delicious silliness.
So, would I recommend this game? Eh, it's fun. If you've got money to burn or, like me, you love Saints Row to the point of unhealthiness, you'll enjoy it. Just, not for very long.
I would suggest getting it on sale, because otherwise it will feel like a bit of a ripoff. I got it as a present so I really can't complain.
They really should have a "suggested minimum discount before purchase" or something, for reviews.
I'd say a game like this is worth 10 bucks. 15 if you're feeling generous.

Why penalize players for not wanting to do the tutorials? It seemed to me that I did not receive money for those because I skipped them (been playing MtG since Tempest) and a player doesnt seem to be able to go back and do them for the reward.
I have to say I like the pace of the game, that's probably the strongest feature here, but the client is unbearably flaky. It crashes every day or two, completely freezes requiring restart every twenty to fourty minutes, and the client will minimise randomly. It often minimised for me at key moments when I'd have liked to stop the timer to play an ability or spell in response to my opponent. (Sucks pretty badly losing your regenerate creatures when you had approximately a million untapped land and nothing else to do with it! :c ) I've also noticed that it sometimes takes an age and a half to get into a random two-headed giant match because somehow the game you were connecting to is "full" or some such nonsense, and so is the next one, and the next one, and...
I'd like to give it a neutral rating, as it's definitely not a bad game, but a lot of that has to do with it being MtG and not the implementation of the game. Sadly, I have to vote for a no at the present time. It's close to being mediocre or even above par, but just I can't abide losing to silly game system hiccups.
Do take note of the time this review is posted when reading it. The problems may get dealt with in a future patch, but I'm personally done with this for now. :c

As such, you trade the visceral excitement of being super-Rambo extraordinaire in favor of a more intellectual approach to taking out a tenement full of skeezy lowlives.
It's funny how this game truly captures the
of Call of Duty "shoot and cover" gameplay in a minimalist 8-bit package. Your slide button slips you into cover but also brings a certain factor of CQC into the mix, allowing executions on enemies reloading from cover. The graphics are dirt simple but it's the same gameplay principles as next-gen shooters, and that alone makes for a subtly enriching experience.
I really wish this game had better rewards. I've just completed level 13 War on Drugs with all challenges using... Clive. Clive is a reward character unlocked by completing all previous levels with all challenges, so he should be mega-badass, right? Wrong. I spent more than two hours on that stage and only managed to succeed thanks to some opportune weapon drops. There's a dearth of design space in this game, and the plethora of playable characters doesn't hide the fact that there's limited ways to play. There's only three buttons to this game in the first place, all the characters and the rewards only feel like a distraction!
I feel like this game went largely unnoticed because it doesn't have the camp and explosiveness of its immediate competitor and that this is to the gaming world's detriment. I blame marketing, mostly. The store page is rather misleading, with all the story elements glossing over the true nature of your purpose. The title explicitly states you are
but no one ever tells you what you are. Turns out you are just as much of a deranged murdering psychopath as your enemies; basically the same as the protagonists from BroForce. In effect,
is essentially funny accents over funny explosions. A puzzle game with guns. You end up blasting just as many hadjis as in that other game so no point being so goddamn cryptic about it! Just say what your game is about and people will appreciate the superior gameplay of your product and maybe even savor the minimalist duck and shoot experience.
ADDENDUM: Play with a gamepad, keyboard controls are unusable.

As of writing this review, I have two levels left of Not A Hero, but I just can't bring myself to finish them. While Not A Hero is fun for an hour or two, it quickly gets incredibly repetitive. It all comes down to this; after the novelty of the cool concept goes away, this game gets incredibly boring.
Much like in Hotline Miami (which shares the same publisher as Not A Hero), you'll constantly be dying and restarting in this game. This is the games biggest flaw. Unlike in Hotline Miami, I never felt motivated to continue. The gameplay itself is slow, save for the first few levels. You and your enemies can take multiple hits, which makes the game impossible to speed through like you would in HM. Because of that, I never felt that rush to jump right into another try. I just felt so...bleh. After 2 hours, i felt like I was doing the same levels over and over again with no variety. I also never felt satisfied with my deaths. In HM, I always feel like my deaths were fair and occured because I made a mistake. However, in NAH, I felt like all of my deaths were the game's fault, not mine. The cover system, which is the main selling point of this game, just feels unfinished. I'll tap the buttin to go into cover, only to stop a litltle short, which I won't realize until an enemy fills me with bullets.
The game tries to create some variety by giving you different characters to play as, but about halfway through the game, you're almost required to use one of the shotgun characters, Cletus or Mike, in order to take out the late game bullet sponges. This game also really could have benefitted from some good music. Instead, you get to listen to one of the most bland soundtracks of all time.
I applaud Roll7 for trying to make you unique game, but Not A Hero just gets too repetitive and boring. If a sequel is ever made with faster, twitch gameplay and more variety, I'll be first in line to get it, but for now, I'd stay away from this game.

Final Fantasy XIII is a gorgeous looking game set in an unique fantasy world and offering six characters to create your battle team of three from. But while it present itself as a role play game the only thing you will be doing is fighting battles ad nausea. You might call it a grind fest even, where it not for the fact that any fluid gameplay is undone by a milliard of cut scenes. Sometimes a cut scene will follow another and even another before control is handed back to you and you might find out that you just barely walked a minute or fought one short battle before you get inflicted by another series of cut scenes. There might even be a nice story underneath the hood, but after a zillion cutscenes it gets so tedious that I started to skip them just to get on with the game.
What story I followed is basically over-the-top-soap style drama because everyone has either lost someone, has an axe to grind or has some other chip on her or his shoulder. So while you are fleeing your pursuers or preparing to attack them everyone takes and has ample time for their own personal tragedies and everything is told in no subtle way: it is Drama with a captal D.  The kind that has people staring in the camera, run away in anguish or slink down to the floor in desperation. The only character I liked was Fang because she wasn't moaning all the time and felt more mature than the rest. But I fear it was in the make. However I quitted the game, perhaps on purpose, so I can live in the fantasy that she isn't a moaner like the rest of the cast.
Once the story no longer offers any entertainment what is left is combat. Besides preparing your team for battle there is zero choice in the game. Dialogs you can only watch, there is one way to go, your teams are a given or fixed for a long time. Swapping members in an out, at times forced upon you by the game, causes your prepared tactics(called paradigms) to  be wiped out. Battles last in general for like 60 seconds, while preparing for for them feels like far too long as you have to navigate superfluous menus. For one thing, the game has like six online shops all selling their own items, so why not just have one shop selling it all saving you the bother to have to check them all? And why not just do the upgrading of you equipment in the same menu as these shops, instead of forcing you to go to another menu for upgrades?
Improving your characters is also limited. Their upgrade paths are linear and while you get eventually to unlock all roles for all characters some roles are just better suited for a specific character because he or she gets all the special upgrades while the others linger behind due to the lack of them.
All in all it's a nice game to look at, but just doesn't capture my attention to last till the end.

Hitman: Absolution, a stealth game where you play in the role of agent 47, an assassin.
It is really a fun game, and unlike the previous game, you really had a storyline instead of killing of certain targets. This made the game, for me atleast, a lot more interesting to do. But on the other hand, just like with the assassin's creed series, I somehow prefer the idea of 'You-have-one-target-and-find-a-way-to-kill-him'. I missed this in the campaign itself, but with the second gamemode, Contracts, they made up for it.
The campaign:
It truly is a good campaign, it really keeps you attention as you try to figure out what is happening and try to solve your problems while you sneak past countless enemies and killing them one by one in silence. You also can pick up weapons to unlock them in Contracts.
Contracts:
This was probably the best about the entire game. You, a friend, or just any person can go into any level of the campaign and create targets, so creating a contract. But you just don't say like "kill that target", making the levels impossible, you really have to play through the level, kill the targets you want to kill and set your own highscore for others to beat. So not only will you show them that it is possible to do, you also show them that they can do better. This truly is amazing. But I have to warn, some people that are really good at this game can make near-impossible levels with near-impossible scores, which can be frustrating. But other than that, this gamemode is really, really fun.
Gameplay:
Just like any other stealth game, you walk around crouched, sneak around enemies and then kill them. You can even dress in a certain uniform to hide in plain sight, but when you behave suspiciously or enter prohibed areas for that uniform, the enemy will question you and eventually kill you.

Attention fellow gamers!
After just 17 hours me and my friend finished a single playthrough of the game in co-op. We discovered something: this game is a must in co-op! We had loads of fun and we were frustrated more than once when we couldn’t kill a boss or troll. But in the end we got through and concluded that this game is more than awesome!! On the other hand we were let down by the final battle, which was simply tooooooo easy, since we had more difficulty defeating the first boss in the game.
THE STORY: We were pleasantly surprised by the fact that the story is interwoven with the actual storyline of LOTR. You even come across characters as Aragorn, Gandalf, Lord Elrond, Legolas and Gloin (known from the Hobbit-trilogy) and even Frodo and Bilbo Baggins. You follow three companions (Eradan, Andriel and Farin) on their quest to defeat a minion of the dark lord Sauron. On their way they make several friends and stops in the north of Middle Earth.
GRAPHICS: Not bad at all for a game that is already 4 years old. We saw a fair amount of detail on armours, buildings and the like and didn’t realise we were playing such an old game.
INTERFACE: Convenient use of hotkeys and a useful minimap! The inventory was a little off, since you had very limited
space and images for additional and trivial objects in the world of Middle Earth.
GAMEPLAY: We found it very useful that you could see the name of your friends on screen even if they were in an entirely different place/room. A very useful feature of the game is that you have the option to exchange items with other players that are only suitable for that particular race. Conveniently enough there several sell/buy/return to civilisation-points.
-	For the Ranger: Very smooth movement of the character during a fight and one of the current reviewers enjoyed the swordplay a little too much at times. We liked the convenient switch between two-handed, one-handed, dual wielding and bow very useful. And, contrary to some other RPG’s,  the realism of being attacked whilst you are looting or switching weapons was very satisfactory to us! We loved the critical, brutal, legendary, etc. strikes with the swords and headshots with the bow too. They lead to some pretty funny ways of dying! We would’ve loved an alternative attack with hotkey ‘2’ while using a two-handed sort, but that could just be because we didn’t unlock every skill in the skill tree.
-	For the Lore-master: Andriel has some great abilities to use in combat, as a supportive mage. For example, she can conjure a magical shield that can protect you against arrows and magical blasts. She also can use her staff as a melee weapon, that is actually quite strong. Because of her Elven ancestry, Andriel can use herbs to fabricate potions to support herself or her companions. This can be decisive at some points in the game.
-	For the Champion: Not applicable (yet), but Farin is awesome!! He got us out of trouble more than once…more like a thousand times…LOL.
Overall conclusion: ‘Lord of the rings: War in the north’ is a must if you are a fan over LOTR, RPG and/or co-op gaming. We had hours and hours of fun (and yet more to come on Heroic and Legendary difficulty) and we didn’t get bored with the storyline once. And once again: THIS GAME IS AWESOME!! *No addiction what so ever* Hahahahaha!!
Enjoy the game!

I wanted to like this game, I love 2d atmospheric platformers, but I just can't get over the combat system and the laborious exploration. But first I should say its not a bad game because it works, there is so much junk on steam these days that is just broken half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥asset flip junk...but Hollow Knight works, the controls work, the characters are interesting and the art and music is very good.
However... the problems:
Problem ONE: Combat...at least the melay combat
-My main problem is that to hit an enemy you character must be facing towards them, however because there is no lock on system this means that you must actually point your character towards them with the joystick, WHY is this a problem?...well because taking a hit means touching pixes with and enemy and there are NO invisibility frames, which means when fighting, to swing and hit an enemy you mostly need to be moving towards it at the same time, thus to fight without taking hits you must move towards and enemy time your swing so that you hit it and knock it back just before your pixels touch, then do a quick run backwards so you have time to move in again and time you swing just before you collide...because there are no iFrames even if you land a hit you cant really press forward on enemies while beating on them or you will just start taking damage.......The end result is combat where you run in swing then run away and repeat till you die of bordom, it takes away any sense of agression and make you feel like the game is just flatly prohibiting you from forcing the combat beyond the peck and retreat pace that it seems to proscribe.
-My other problem with the combat and its more or personal preference is that its based on pixels touching...it contributes to making the combat really slow and defensive with many enemies, you are always in fear of getting touched, which mostly annoying, its much more exciting to go after enemies and worry about coutering or defending against there attacks...not O NO my character model brushed there character model when I tried to jump.
Problem Two: The exploration
-The game looks nice and the things you find and characters you meet are cool, but I'm sorry as much as this game wants to be Dark Souls it isn't. Having very limited fast travel and save points forcing me to do a ton of back tracking is just tedious, boring, and ponderous. Dark Souls is an ornate world with most of the geometry of a level being unique and recognizable and it fun to explore levels enough to get intimatly familiary with a set piece and know all the paths that can be taken, and the game forces you to do this somewhat because of required back  tracking....but Im sorry Hollow Knight your art is nice but its still just typical 2d cave.dungeon/tunnel stuff its not that interesting I don't care to learn the layout of a stupid little cave maze, nobody says or man rember that one awesome tunnel that turns left then right! Exploring is fine, but it seems to be forced on you to a degree that is not warrented by the set pieces.
ps. There is not much for puzzles, if you expected some in a 2d platformer, this game is all about combat to progress not puzzles.

There are limitless ways to pass judgement upon your enemies. The "kill" or "subdue" animations are also well done. Being able to retrieve an disguise has always been a big part of the franchise. It's a lot of fun, don't get me wrong, flying around on demon wings and shooting demons with stake throwing shotguns straight out of Painkiller is a blast, but the game feels empty.
The characters barely speak, only Dane Vogel and the DeWinter sisters (as if we were missing those two incredibly secondary and uninteresting characters, one of which originally dies after having barely a line of her own and the other partly responsible for devouring an unreasonable amount of budget for SRIII that could've gone to better writing instead of stupid casting choices like Sasha Grey or Hulk Hogan) make a comeback from previous games, aside for the two main characters, and the lack of homies make it so that banter is impossible.
The cutscenes are hilarious and somewhat meta, and the style and setup of the plot are the usual SR fare, as in "we're having fun writing this, you'll have fun reading it", too bad in 4 hours of play I must have gotten 4 in total, and i have the feeling the next will be either the last or the one before because, spoiler, there are basically no plot missions and the next plot point i'm given, first time that I get to pick when to start a plot mission in the whoole game, is "Crash the wedding".
Each cutscene is somewhat related to a special event that starts just after it, then you're back to side activities until an arbitrary point when you've accomplished enough that the game feels like you deserve another slice of delicious silliness.
So, would I recommend this game? Eh, it's fun. If you've got money to burn or, like me, you love Saints Row to the point of unhealthiness, you'll enjoy it. Just, not for very long.

Rivals of Aether is an amazing game. I played a lot of Super Smash Bros with my friends casually, and had so much good fun with it. One problem I always had with Super Smash Bros was the moves didn't feel heavy. In this game, which has a similar style to Super Smash Bros, does not have this problem. Each hit feels like it counts, and parrying is a smooth and skill based mechanic, which I prefer over shielding. It also has coding for things like wave dashing so it can get very mechanical to play, but is still smooth and not wonky. This game can and will take hours of your life away.
Pros:
-Coded well, so has few bugs
-Great U.I. with smooth menu transitions
-Amazing character kits that flow well together
-Well balanced character roster (Basically anyone can be super op, well maybe minus Maypul (Rip Maypul))
-Great tutorial for beginners and experts
-Good control layout and custimization
-Character and skin customization
-Great community
-Premium skins if you want to burn some money (They look really nice)
-Active developers so content is being added regularly
-Fun and interesting story mode
-Special rewards and skins for people who attent offical tournaments or follow social media
-A good and scaling AI system
-Controller support
-Online multiplayer
Cons:
-Will take numerous hours away from your life (I have 73 hours but another 70+ playing locally at friend's houses)
-Peer to peer connection (This can be a problem, but it makes sense for the size of the development team and the style of the game)
-Limited character roster, 8 to be exact. (However, the characters are done amazingly and more characters will be consistanly added)
Overall I would personally say this is a great game for both casual and competitive players, that is well worth $15. Also, playing with friends is really fun, I personally don't like online play that much. Seriously though, there is no better way to play this game than getting 4+ friends together and playing all night, while blasting music.

This is an amazingly intricate game where you get to experience what it feels like to survive in war. Although, I must say, that previous phrase is a huge understatement.
The amount of necessary evil you have to do in order to survive is saddening to the point that it pretty much depressed me, made me experience extremely weird mood swings and made me feel like a monster, a beast with the mind of a psychopath.
At some point into the game you start questioning just why the heck are you playing this game. What is it that you get out of it other than a crappy day and sadness. You try so hard to stop playing, but you find yourself unable to. You start thinking, what would happen to these people if I left the game? Could they survive just fine?
This War of Mine is an absolutely fascinating and beautifully crafted game that is a strong and solid eye-opener. It makes you see things in a different light, it makes you sad, it makes you happy for giving that kid the meds he needs for his mother, it makes you feel villanous for having to steal, it makes you feel disgusted with yourself for having to kill; but most importantly it makes you feel just what kind of a stinking, ugly, disgusting thing the war is.
Did I also say all of these happened within 3 hours of me playing? My heart and brain couldn't stand any longer, I had to take a break...
It's amazing. Just buy it. Really.

Slightly disappointing.
Visually, it's nice but confusing. In the Civ series, a Horse resourse looks like a horse, Bananas look like bananas, etc. But what the hell is Chitin or Reslin? Trying to remember what they all look like is going to take some serious time.
In terms of gameplay, it very much resembles SMAC (for those of you old enough to remember that brilliant product). Limited to a handful of "nations" (instead of the 30+ from Earth-based Civ), I can see this getting boring much sooner than the standard Civ games. Likewise, the "miasma" (i.e. SMAC "xenofungus") acts as more of an annoyance than as a hazard.
Honestly, SMAC was a much better product: you could change land elevations, tailor your units as you saw fit (my favorite was the Drop Grav Supply), and win multiple different victory types. Anyone notice there's no such thing as a Diplomatic Victory in this one?
That said, this is a Civ product. It plays like a Civ product. And if you enjoy the Civilization series, you'll like this one.
Caveat: from the promotional releases, I was under the impression that this was going to be an entirely knew concept of Civilization. When it comes right down to it, all they've added -- added, mind you, and not redesigned -- is linear missions with linear choices. Yes, the tech tree is now a web, but it is a very linear web in many ways.
My grades:
If you've never played any Civ game: 5 out of 5
If you've played at least one Civ game: 3.5 out of 5
If you've played SMAC: 3 out of 5
Overall as a gaming product: 4 out of 5
There's a lot more I could say about this one; a few positives, but mostly negative. However, this is just a review, and not a masters thesis.

Alright. Take a look at my hours. In this short amount of time, I can review this game with confidence.
I'd like to start off by saying that this is easily one of, if not THE best survival games I've ever played.
Now it's not a survival in the sense of minecraft, DAYZ, the forest, rust, etc.
In this case, survival means the most literal sense of the word, staying alive.  When a character dies, they are dead, and stay that way. A nice perma-death feature keeps you on your game.
You are trying to survive (and live...or continue living) in a war ravaged city. You need to hunt for food, medicine, things to keep you warm, weapons, and other survivors, well the ones that don't want to kill you...or raid your house while you're out...
This game does not hold your hand, it's gritty, it puts you in an environment, and into situations where you actually need to think about what to do with your short time with the cover of darkness. It tugs at your morals, and makes you think things you don't want to.
Is it worth going to the supermarket, knowing there are armed bandits, to get food because we are out? OR do we need to trade away our supplies for medicine, to save a woman and her children?
Every decision matters, try not to make bad ones....your game may end faster than it started.
BUT, you can always start over, make different decisions, kill (or help) more people, blah blah...
So with all that, I highly recommend this game if you are into any sort of survival, fight for your life game.

I love Civilization - have spent hours on versions III, IV and V - so when "Beyond Earth" came out, I had to buy it. If you like Civ, you will probably like BE. However, it's not as good. The Civs draw a lot of their depth from actual Earth civilizations.  We know what the Eiffel tower is, and the Pyramids - so it means something to build them. Bonus when you build them where they actually belong. You know what it means to discover gunpowder or the printing press. Beyond Earth has much the same game play, but without the subtance the comes from using real history.
They tried. They really did.  You can take your planet's colony in one of three very distinct directions, with different philosophies towards alien life and Earth's past. This is plausible and interesting.  There is a variety of planet type, with respect to water formation and climate.  You get lively quotes from the leaders every time you research a new technology, which brings the personalities of the founding colonists to light. But it never quite manages to have the drama of the original Civ series.
In spite of this, I enjoy playing the game. VIsually, it is beautifully drawn. And I can usually win without stressing myself. The soundtrack deserves special mention. You can download it separately and enjoy it on  its own.  Wonderful music!
I recommend Beyond Earth, to gamers who like turn based strategy games. It's not the best of its kind, but it's very good.

I was mildly surprised to find Bioshock Remastered in my library the other day, so I gave it a whirl.  I played all three Bioshock games on the PS3, but Bioshock was my favorite (for obvious reasons), and when I heard about a remastered edition, I wasn’t exactly stoked.  It seems every release nowadays are just remastered ports and HD rereleases of older games.  Bioshock seems to have aged gracefully from what I remember, the PC port was never hard on the eyes, so I felt that a remastered edition was unnecessary unless it was something of an overhaul.  Needless to say the Remastered edition is essentially an update to the original, but with a few surprises and business decisions that make this whole thing better than what others have done in the past.
Graphically, this one looks almost exactly the same as the original, only with some curves being more rounded and better textures.  The bad thing is that the game will eat up a tad over 21 GB compared to the 6 GB of the original (Though that could also be due partially with the next point).
In addition to the game, the new version includes Directors Commentary (each part of which needs to be found within the game as reels), the Museum of Orphaned Concepts , and the PS3 Challenge Rooms, which are, as expected, puzzles of a sort that force you to be creative to solve a problem, and Survivor Difficulty (also from the PS3 port).  Not to mention trading cards and achievements for those who want the validation of progress, I guess.
The remastered editions both seem to have replaced the original ones in the steam store, and those who have the game already will receive it for free, which is not bad. I’m also somewhat surprised that they’re 20 bucks instead of a full 60.
As mentioned before, Bioshock was about 6 GB, while the remastered is about 21 GB thanks to the content and retextures, and the graphics aren’t improved or overhauled in anyway aside from some minor things and textures.  Also they seem to have quite a bit of bugs from the get go and lack of graphics settings (which seem to have been fixed now apparently).  More than anything, the PC remasters are nothing more than just updated versions with a bit of extra content.
If you haven’t bought it yet, you can’t really go wrong.  Bioshock is a great game with some decent writing (though I do have some minor reservations, but hey, it’s the Remastered version people want to know about).

And that's exactly what this game is, a gigantic black hole. You'll start playing, 7 hours will pass. You'll get a text, go to reply, and notice it's been 10 minutes. I love this game; however, I must admit, being an ardent fan of the Super Smash Bros fighting games renders me a bit biased. For the sake of objectivity, I won't hold back from my more critical opinions of some of the games detriments. Firstly, if you have a predilection for fast-paced, combo/string heavy fighting games with an emphasis on skill, then go ahead and buy the game; it's great in that aspect. In comparison to Smash Bros, Rivals harbors that swift, intense feeling of Melee (offering welcome familiarity), as well as manipulating the cardinal rock paper scissors mind-game that is at the core of Smash. Smash can be broken down into its most rudimentary form: switching between shield, grab, or attack options. The shield from Smash is now replaced in Rivals by a parry; this requires more precision, reminiscent of a perfect shield in Smash. The parry, if timed precisely when an enemy hits your hit box, will temporarily stun the attacking enemy. This allows for a major follow-up that could even lead to a kill. I think this parry mechanic gives the game a fresh feel. If it was a blatant copy of Smash, the game would be insipid and one would quickly grow blasé. However, the combo intensive gameplay, small maps, and parry mechanics make the game feel more aggressive; therefore, unique from Smash in a fun, aggro way. However, because the game is so intense, it's arduous for newcomers to fighting games to get into the game. Techniques such as DI (directional influence) and techs (parries at the ground when being hit onto a surface) are essential to preempt early deaths. I'm terrible at both, and find myself struggling when faced against players with more prowess at the game. The game's major issue is it's lack of accessibility. Most everyone playing the game at the moment is playing it competitevly. I love the competitive atmosphere, though, would prefer if the playerbase was widened so that the game doesn't feel so punishing all the time. This could be ameliorated by creating more "for fun" type modes to mess around in. Also, I frequently have latency issues when playing online. People's ping is at an egregious high and the lag makes an already onerous competitive fighting experience even more difficult to handle. Hopefully this will be patched soon. I still love the game, but find that it has nothing more to offer than a competitive fighting experience. The story is banal and the AI is asinine during the short story missions. It was cool to see where the characters originated, though, it offered nothing more than that knowledge of mythos. Regardless of my complaints, I truly appreciate what the developers have done: they captured the quintessence of Smash whilst adding a more intense feel to the flow of the game. I look forward to decimating the AI more and then going online to get destroyed by actual people lol. I learn more and more every time and it's a great experience to see your skills enhance the more you discover about the game.

I very much enjoyed the first installment of Bioshock and had stayed away upon hearing the cries of "meh" about this sequel. I'm ashamed to say that I missed out by waiting so long to purchase this game. This game likely suffers from high expectations from the first one. I'll admit that compared side to side that the original is likely a superior game from a storyline perspective, although not by much.
The combat was fun, especially with the drill charge (love that move), your character had believable motivation for what he was doing, the story was engaging and didn't have a meh twist like the original Bioshock. As a matter of fact, there really wasn't some "twist" or weird stuff with the story. Provided you listened to the diaries along the way, you got to see both sides of every character's story. Each story had two faces and you could plainly see the motivations for every character.
I recommend this highly if you enjoyed the original Bioshock.

The atmosphere of the game is designed well: the cityscape is sufficiently hellish and the vehicles are all modified slightly in appearance and name, and sometimes function too. It's great fun to hop in a Comet, press E to set it on fire, and then drive along a main road for as long as you can before you explode. Encountering a Rambulance is also great for a laugh too, when you see them swerving all over the road aiming for pedestrians to hit. Finally you can go on a monster truck rampage and crush cars all over the road.
I only wish they had added more quirky vehicles challenges like these.

for such little content¹. I still haven’t played the original game, and I bought this title since in the description it says that it’s a good introduction of the world of

This title consists in two short episodes: two girls called Lycoris and Aoi who are agents of an organization called Rubina. The girls dress as nuns and they kill vampires, in order to protect innocent people.
Then there’s a few semi romantic scenes and dialogue between them, both characters insist that they love each other, but “not like that”. There’s some fanservice because of it, which I liked. The ending was pretty abrupt tho, things were getting cute and it ended faster before I could even say “Aww—“. lol
The second story is very different, some sort of sci-fi mixed with an occult group trying to take over the power. A woman called Iris together with her colleagues, Aconite and Galega
, take down these crazy guys that are part of the occult group that want people to get infected with an impure life force. Wow.
5/10. The art style together with BGM and VA are pretty good, but honestly, the price tag bothers me a lot. Lycoris and Aoi’s story where a good introduction to the original game (at least you get to know a bit of the plot), and Iris route was basically for fanservice. Which is fine, but just… If you haven’t played the original game yet, how can this second story be considered a “good introduction to the original”? Even so, it was fun. The ending was unexpected at least. Overall, I recommend to get this title AFTER you read Libra of the Vampire Princess, and only if you liked the story a lot in order to pay an absurd amount of money on two short kinetic novels. You can always wait for a good sale too, it’s up to you.

This is an interesting title. When you look at it from a distance it seems like your typical RPG from Square Enix. However, once you get closer to it, you start to notice that it's not so typical after all...
This is mostly due to the combat system being rather unique in the way how you control groups or "Unions", as they are called in the game, instead of your typical four person party.
The battles have turns, and you can take as much time as you like to decide what you're going to do. But because I'm a lazy person, I'm not going to get too much in depth with how the unions work exactly. Forgive me.
Anyways... Controls are okay for such a old port from a console game(You may want to tweak the controls a bit when playing with keyboard and mouse), and I really haven't got anything negative to say about the visuals of the game. Again pretty solid looking for a five year old game.
Soundtrack is what you'd expect from a JRPG. Not really much to say about it.
For some unknown reason however, listening to the english voice acting was like torture for me. Thankfully all I had to do, was go into to the settings and set the voice acting to be japanese aswell as put english subtitles on.
As for the story, it's a bit generic and predictable. But then again I haven't finished the game yet so there might be some plot twists hiding along the way. At the very least, I hope there are some unpredictable events coming.
All and all this is a game worth picking up if you have some pocket money and wish to play a JRPG with a twist. Let me warn you though. This game isn't easy, especially if you go in blind.

TL;DR: a sweet and action packed moba with short rounds and interesting ability upgrades that deserves to be bigger than it is.
I got this way back in 2016. I liked it, got the hero pack, but didn't really commit because I had Smite to fullfill my moba needs at the time. I've dropped smite a while ago because the game is getting too needy and since developed a tickleling need to play something moba-ish. The recent sale reminded me about BR and I decided to give it another shot. And it stuck. The game is already very fun and quite balanced considering the nature of these types of games, but you can just sense the potential lurking underneath the surface. Strangely, besides the solid modes and gameplay already there, it feels this game could do with alot more content, especially more heroes. Mind you this is not a complaint. It's a longing for more. More Battlerite in different ways and even more depth. More ways of fixing matches and customizing games. I love the reward system in the game; it's generous and makes you keep coming back. The grind is just right. The way the character skill upgrades work is that it gives each character a different flavour of playstyle without compromising the core gameplay of the class. You get to pick 1 out of 3 upgrades from a tier each new round. The tooltip shows what kind of upgrade it is; control, mixed, damage, support. Simple and effective. All in all I really recommend this game!

Crysis is this game.
Crysis Warhead is a psuedo sequel, the same time frame played from your buddy's perspective.
Crysis Wars is defunct multiplayer.
Crysis 2 is the proper sequel but plays very differently than the above.
Crysis 3 (and 4) are on "Origin" not Steam.
Background:
Crysis was the benchmark in PC graphics for a very long time.  It's 2016 and this game still looks fairly decent.  Probably the first game I've ever played where a forest feels like a real forest.  Way ahead of its time and most people's hardware.  Unfortunately it also missed out on a lot of optimization potential that later games got right.  Even with a GTX 970 with comparable SSD+processor this game loads slowly and did have issues in an aerial sequence.  I had settings almost maxed (keep that motion blur disabled thanks) except for the aerial bit.  The UI is terrible and every session I had to put fullscreen back on.
Gameplay:
This is an oldschool first person military shooter with sandbox elements and regular cut scenes.  You start off with all suit powers (hold middle click and drag in a direction):
- default is armor which includes faster health regen
- then cloak is overpowered (drains power as you move and drops if you attack) yet fails at melee range.
- strength makes you jump higher and absorb more falling damage
- speed makes you run faster, really fast for a short time
Good to know stuff:
Falling damage can kill (use strength to minimize).  The suit lets you breath underwater.  There's also a separate night vision that drains a separate power meter.  Armored vehicles require explosives to destroy.  You can only carry three kinds of weapons at a time, but can swap on the fly and recall a previous weapon's ammo pool (which is the only reason to swap late game).  Health is regenerative but the meter is on screen.  In this iteration, ammo pickups are totally manual.  Crouch and fully prone are separate functions.  WHENEVER YOU GET IN A VEHICLE HIT F1 FOR THIRD PERSON!  No achievements or collectibles, just secondary objectives with no impact aside from providing another ammo cache.  Relatively short compared to today's titles (9-15 hours).
Verdict:
Crysis was a great game in its time.  It's an oldschool precursor to the Call of Duty franchise.  But if that's what you're hoping for, you won't enjoy this.  The game is fairly unforgiving (though stealth is an obvious option) and there are a few really annoying aspects.  Ammo, enemy, and suit power management are a must.  Play on easy if you are at all worried, you will still die a bunch.  It's polished but not streamlined; if you played any of the other games (which included many quality of play improvements) you might want to skip this one.
Psuedo spoilers "what are you getting into":
The game has several innovative sequences, but that could also be a source of frustration as the game starts off almost sandbox then gets fairly linear.  The game shifts in tone and even play style half way through, leading me to miss the earlier sections of assaulting Korean bases.  The ending absolutely has a nice final boss for a climax, but then acts like one of the next games will pick up your character's life a few minutes later.  They don't, making that sort of a cliffhanger.
Bottom line:  Worth $4

The core mechanic - "Battle Rank" system is poorly executed. The more monsters you kill, the higher your battle rank goes. This War of Mine is a well thought-out, emotionally investing game about the struggles of civilians in a civil war. Caught in the crossfire between rebels and the military, you play a small group of survivors that must stick together and make it through to the end of the war.
Positive notes
-Character diversity: Each character you can have in your group has different capabilities. One might be a good cook. One might be good at lifting everyone's spirits. One might be completely useless altogether. The characters also have differing opinions and will react differently to situations. One might approve of taking from another group of survivors, while another might actually get depressed.
-Tension building: When you go out to scavenge, things are immediately tense. You have a limited time to get what you can find and get out. There might be other survivors who won't be fond of your presence. You might even have to force yourself to fight military occupants.
-Resource Management: You have to manage your resources. This might mean characters will go hungry for a while. This might mean the guy with the less severe wounds waits while you patch up the girl with the stab wounds. Being prepared is difficult with so little resources, and with people who'll try to steal from you on a near nightly basis, it's always difficult to simply stock up. This is a good thing, it makes resources more valuable to you.
-Past Reliances: Characters may have things that were luxuries before the war. One of your characters might be a smoker, one might need a cup of coffee in the morning. If these characters don't get their addictions they'll be affected, but the things they take (Cigarettes, coffee, alcohol, those sorts of things) are also valuable, so one may find themselves with one less bottle of moonshine to trade off because the group alcoholic just finished downing it.
Negative notes
-Luck of the draw: Everything relies on a sort of luck of the draw system; you'll need to be lucky to be able to find the resources you need, which sucks for someone like me, whose luck is awful. I've gone through a looong time without food, only to get it, feed everyone, and then get robbed, forcing you to try and find bandages for your fed group's newfound bulletholes.
-Item value: Your items are less valuable than the trader's items. This is a fact you will have to face. You would think that, with people who smoke, you could trade a cigarette to a guy for a bottle of water. No; that water's more valuable. You'll always need to trade more and feel like you're getting ripped off. Fortunately, there's a character who can get you a good deal that you can even begin the game with.
Overview
I love this game. It's well thought-out, it's got great pacing, and best of all (If you're into reading), it gives you a reason to hate the war that's gripped this city. It makes you think about the hard decisions; do you rob the elderly couple who can barely walk just so you can survive? Or do you leave them alone and try somewhere else tomorrow?
Overall, I give this game a solid 8 out of 10.

I believe that this game, Civilization: Beyond Earth, was a complete waste of time waiting for, and earned money. First of all, I do not hate the game, I dislike it.
The concept for the game was marvelous. You, as a future nation who has risen above the others, travels to alien planet to colonize as Earth is overpopullated and resources run dry. As you land, you are thrown straight away into new terrain. Large ravines stretching across the horizon to the alien nests. You must choose what to do with the new species found: live with them in harmony (accpeting them and their culture), stay away from them and form a new earth, or dominate them with brutal force. It was an amazing idea.
But, then came the game itself. As I started my first game, with two other friends, we were amazed by the graphical update from Civilization V, and wanted this to take its predecessor's position. We wandered the alien planet, trying new nations, and racing each other to wonders. It looked like it would be the new Brave New World.
We were quickly proved wrong. While the early game was excellent, the middle to late game really fell short. Wonders were sparse and most units were obsolete. Units would destroy capitals in one shot, and aliens stood no chance to the humans.
**NOTE** One of the largest problems in the game is the alien world's version of happiness. Health. Unless you focus primarily on health through the entire game, you will end up in the negatives. Health is too important to lose, but other things rival it.
After many hours of gameplay and close judgment, I come to the rating of 6.5/10.
May Civilization: Beyond Earth have it's own Brave New World, or I fear it will fall into my "Trash Games" folder.

This is an amazingly intricate game where you get to experience what it feels like to survive in war. Although, I must say, that previous phrase is a huge understatement.
The amount of necessary evil you have to do in order to survive is saddening to the point that it pretty much depressed me, made me experience extremely weird mood swings and made me feel like a monster, a beast with the mind of a psychopath.
At some point into the game you start questioning just why the heck are you playing this game. What is it that you get out of it other than a crappy day and sadness. You try so hard to stop playing, but you find yourself unable to. You start thinking, what would happen to these people if I left the game? Could they survive just fine?
This War of Mine is an absolutely fascinating and beautifully crafted game that is a strong and solid eye-opener. It makes you see things in a different light, it makes you sad, it makes you happy for giving that kid the meds he needs for his mother, it makes you feel villanous for having to steal, it makes you feel disgusted with yourself for having to kill; but most importantly it makes you feel just what kind of a stinking, ugly, disgusting thing the war is.
Did I also say all of these happened within 3 hours of me playing? My heart and brain couldn't stand any longer, I had to take a break...
It's amazing. Just buy it. Really.

I purchased this game because of the good reviews and the fact that it claimed to be a 'Metroidvania' game, but I'm absolutely dissapointed.
Playability is ok (and that's probably the most important feature of this kind of games), but game design is not as good as you can expect (especially when compared to an 'Igavania' game). The extense map doesn't catch you from the beginning, you don't feel encouraged enough to sneak into the game.
Art is almost monochromatic all the time (well, the game is obviously true-color, but most graphics are focused on just one predominant color and although there isn't nothing wrong with that, is isn't the style I expect for a classic Metroidvania game).
But what made me really disspointed was MUSIC. It is terrible; no background music most of the time, just some boring Kontakt-library made pseudo-orchestral works with no soul, poor harmony or counterpoint and actually very far from any of the excellent OST found on a REAL Metroidvania game (especially the Konami's ones).
Maybe you can find this game interesting after all but DON'T buy it if you are a long-term fan of classic Metroidvania games. It just isn't what you think.

While it certainly isn't the best hack n slash action game you'll ever play, Lord of the Rings: War in the North proved to be a fun game despite its flaws. This game was designed as a multiplayer experience, so you should play with a friend if you can, if not prepare yourself to constant variations is gameplay as you'll have to change characters more often than not. In the end this was not a setback, as each has a slightly different play style so changing characters (ranger, elf, dwarf) proved to be varied and amusing.
This game is first and foremost aimed at Lord of the Rings / Tolkien fans. If you count yourself among those, you'll be satisfied. I played this game as I was reading The Silmarillion again which proved to be a good choice as the story is not focused on the main events at the end of the Third Age but on the fight against the forces of Sauron in the north of Middle Earth. Don't expect Bethesda or Bioware levels of lore in this game, just relax, enjoy the story and focus on what this game does best - combat.
The fights are intense, combos are easy to execute and enemies' limbs fly all over as you chop Orc after Orc. If you want a good hack'n'slash experience, look no further.

Hollow Knight is a terrific metroidvania and game. The asthetic is unique and well done, the soundtrack is eerie and tense, yet solemn when called for.  The gameplay and combat is a great example of mixing out metroidvania/platforming with new concepts like travel points, the 'dark souls death system' and a great new mechanic that I havent seen before where your ability to heal is directly correlated to your ability to do damage so it promotes a more aggressive playstyle.
There certainly is a some cons in the game:
- I felt that some of the areas looked way to similar, some of the enemies were the same with a new skin (as is expected in these titles)
- Whilst I understand that it is a metroidvania and that is part of the genre - I felt there was a little too much backtracking and I disliked that are a certian point of the game they actually made traveling through the map MORE difficult/cumbersome almost as a counter to all the movement-based abilities you've learnt. I just saw that as a bit unnessecary and more of an annoyance than anything else.
- The start of the game is pretty slow and the time it takes you to acquire your first interesting abilities is a bit long, you'll find many people on reddit / forums who tire of the early game and end up quitting. Although I think theyre being a bit harsh and missing out of a great game, its certainly a legitiment criticism.
Overall, a great title that anyone who likes this genre should own. To think it was made successful by a small team and kickstarter yet has this degree of polish is great too.

Personally, I found this expansion to be enjoyable, but with some flaws.  While I had no crashing or glitching problems (the game ran pretty smoothly for me, actually), I didn't care for a few features, such as the following:
-Lack of Story - While the story isn't bad, it isn't fleshed-out enough.  There could've been a lot more put into the story, like more detailed legacy missions (like in Saints Row IV, for example).  What irks me further is that certain characters from past games do make appearances in cutscenes near the end of the game, which could've been made into more missions (I won't delve into too many details since I don't want to spoil).
-Certain Challenges/Achievements - By this point, why would we necessarily need to drive a vehicle?  We have the ability to run faster than nearly every vehicle driving around, not to mention we can fly anywhere we wish.  I also don't like how the monster trucks handle - they're very unwieldly, at least to me.  I also don't even know how to ride a car on a comet - they don't exactly explain that to you in the game.
Well, that's what I didn't like.  Here's what I did like:
-Playing as Johnny Gat - Always did want to play as him.  Sure, there's no customization, but Johnny is just awesome in action.  I also like how he slices and dices enemies with his knives.  That was a nice touch.  Most of his commentary blurbs are pretty funny too.
-Weapons - While I didn't care for certain weapons (such as Last Supper), I really like some of the deadly weapons and plague-related weapons - specifically, the Armchair-A-Geddon, the Exodus 10, the Lil' Croaker, the Gods Hammer, and the Gallows Dodger.  They cause so much carnage!
-Arcane Powers  - I do like what they've done with twisting the powers from Saints Row IV - such as turning enemies to stone, making them bow before you, and creating a vacuum by stomping the ground which sucks in all loose currency lying around.  Watching Imps tackle demons is great too - especially when you decide to blow them up.
-Flying - Oh my God, FLYING.  It's great!  A lot better than SRIV's gliding setup, and its exhilirating.  The wings' look is just icing on the cake.  It's the quickest way to travel in any Saints Row game too, aside from warping using towers.
-Location - While I didn't have a problem with Steelport being in Saints Row IV (I liked exploring and seeing the differences Zinyak put in), New Hades is a nice change.  Sure, it's not as big, but it's something new to explore.  I like all the sadistic stuff too - like the High Fryer Ferris Wheel, for example.  Really makes it feel like you're in a godforsaken place.
-Carnage - Blowing people (well, husks) and demons up is a great way to relieve stress.
In all, I'd recommend this game, if not for the story, but for the gameplay.  There's plenty of carnage to be had, and it's a good expansion to Saints Row IV.  $20 is a tad steep though - I'd say $10-$15 would be a bit more resonable.  Make of that what you will.

Missing the Heart of SR3
While technically this is a new, smaller, map than the last two games despite being reskinned for Hell, and looking very good in that respect, you will find many areas that feel structurally extremely similiar if not directly lifted from the previous games.
Mechanically this is a clone of SR4. Except for flight, all the powers, majority of weapons are the same exact ones you had in SR4 but instead of the source being hacking a virtual world, it is from Lucifers Halo. The names are different but functionally the same for most of them. The anti-power grenades from the previous game are back, but unexplained how it affects the supposedly most powerful artifact in the universe. Chasing down the orbs is back but now they're Sin Orbs. Once your notoriety gets high enough a boss plops down with the same hellfire rain from the last game and basically the same fight mechanics.
Unfortunately with so much same, whats different? Mostly just the look of the map and that you can play as Gat or Kinzie.  Also the introduction of flying is really cool.
But a bigger question is whats lost? For me the most important thing missing is the cultivation of the plot. Despite having some potentially really interesting characters in the game like Shakespeare & Vlad the Impaler there is almost nothing done with them. In lieu of almost any cutscenes in the game a still frame storybook device was used. So every time you expect to some really interesting interaction it cuts to the storybook and everything is summarised for you. No pop music/culture infused action moments
Also gone any type of customization. No private garages or helopads, no customizing vehicles, changing clothes, etc ...
Whereas in previous games you could pick different homies and see their different interactions with one another, you can pick no one here so thats gone. SR4 was full of celebrity homies like Roddy Piper & Keith David with fun interactions.
This is basically the most Soulless version of Saints Row out of the last 3 or more versions. Describing this as basically a collection of the mini games from previous versions is mostly correct. The battle with Satan is weak and arguably much easier than reaching max notoriety.
I recommend this game but not at full price.
Volition, High Voltage whoever is calling the shots, take some time off, take a year or two and make a next gen Saints Row. Another installment like this on an already 4+ year old game engine could sink the franchise

I had great expectations of this game. I preordered it and woke up at 4 am to play it... and got very very disappointed.
The introduction of your first officer is a prime example of most of this game: tacked on!
The new highway system is fun, but once you get to a place that is sparsly populated, you will spend long minutes travelling though each highway segiment.
The rework of how AI and ship commands work leave you manually controlling your ship at all times and with next to no options for controlling your ships. For most players most of the time, the only command you can give your ships is to follow you.
At release, this game had a large number of game-breaking bugs that left me stuck for hours and restarting the game 4 times before i managed to break though them.
The easy to use, easy to find stuff in map present in previous X games has been redesigned and is now extremely awkward and hard to navigate to say the least. It is extremely hard to find a commodity when you are searching for one and even harder to remember the convoluted way to set the station as an objective.
It is very clear that the user interface of this game was build to mainly appeal to game controllers. The layout of UI makes mouse contol nothing short of painful and getting joysticks to work is an art. Don't even think of trying to use a HOTAS.
The combat system and space graphics are extremely good and nothing beats the satisfaction of blowing up a hostile will your guns (which entails the best explosion graphics i have EVER seen). Although many people complain about the cut and paste station interiors, I like them. Sure it isn't as good as we could have hoped but it still give SOME level of personal feel. I would definitely love to go back to the menu system though. The reworked level of activity in space is another big pro and gives the X universe a more awesome feel to it.
Never the less, due to what I have stated here and an endless list of additional issues, this game is a huge leap back from previous titles and should be avoided at all costs. I hope with all my heart that Egosoft learns from this horrific mistake and look forward to the next installment of the X series. Despite X Rebirth, I can't deny that the X series is still my favourite sci-fi space ship sim. I highly recommend that any player go and buy X3 Terran Conflict as well as seriously consider X3 Reunion and X3 Albion Prelude.

This Action-FPS game was released back in November, 2007. But at the time it had some of the best graphics ever for a game of its kind! The main reason behind this was the kickass-German made Crytek engine that used a heavy demand on graphics cards at the time to present lots of new features. Does crytek sound familiar at all? if it does-that is because they also created the first far cry game waay back in 2004!
These kinds of games typically have big expanses of various maps and consists of stealth missions near the start and middle sections but blooms into a beautiful action-set experience with lots of options! (Even some optional quests!). Crysis was no different and delivered a great action game with many new useful features/gameplay mechanics that more than made up for simpified story sequences, crappy nano-suit power (It is the damn future!) and some really dumb AI.
Anyway i dont want to list everything this game offers here! instead ill chop it into clean little pieces and serve you....The Pros and Cons.
+SO many awesome small little additions to gameplay that make a big difference! Some of these include: Your PC's battery level shown, lots more graphics and weapon options at the time, Minimap accuracy with coordinates,  enhanced physics and a deadly shark to stop people from leaving the map! A frickin shark!!
+I really liked the Abilities FOR the nanosuit, but not the Nanosuit itself (Because of numerous energy reasons that ill describe in Cons below) The Cloak, Speed and Strength are used regularly, and for good reason!
+The Story is very strong and warhead fits in very well. The Title really fits the plot! and the "Futuristic spelling" helps a little bit too i guess. No Purposeful emotional scenes or anything  like that, its an action game dammit!
.But the story has got some great seperation between the stealth and action sequences! A calm cutscene to recap what big event just occured, followed by a guerilla-style trespass on an enemy base is a great mix! Basicsally what im trying to say is that the Pacing in this game is very well done.
+The Vehicles
handle very well surprisingly and are easy to control, speaking of that...
+The tutorial is hardly a tuturial and just a slow part of the story that just happens to teach you the controls. Which are simple and very easy to change! (Loads of settings means more gameplay styles to suit more people=potential larger audience)
+Map is big and cut into sections, but that doesnt really matter as you traverse most of the area with ease. Missions take you to several different locations
Dont classify this as an open world game at all! It is very linear like Basically all FPS shooters. It just has a big map for a few missions then changes it for a smaller, denser one And Repeats often.
+Weapons are quite realistic and have noticeable effects with mixed with the nano-suits abilities! Bullpup rifles will have more recoil than the generic AK-47 found often and it will effect your aiming long distance!
+The Way the Story transforms into the action packed shooter with various sci-fi elements attatched it amazing! If you asked me at the start of the game how i thought it would end, i would give a very different answer. But this is good! It means that the story will keep you guessing often while it introduces new Things to you.
+I couldnt talk about the pros without mentioning the Graphics that it possesses, it is has lots of technical features that i could fill the list with but instead ill give you this
Basically with mods it can run at 8k 60fps and all that good stuff. But remember this is extremely specific to most people. Depends if you care enough about it to mod the games really. But without it, it is definetely impressive
+Enemies are difficult at times, and can be placed in such environments to even give some peope a fright!
+Speaking of Difficulty...Try Delta! it really changes the game and makes you appreciate corners and baricades more than parts of the environment!
-Below-average boss battles, with repetitive strategies to defeat them.
-The AI in this game is quite dumb and found some soliders running into walls, ignoring me throwing grenades and even firing their guns randomly! (Who are they recruiting?).
-The games "maps" are surprisingly linear as i said above and you are contantly reminded of this if you go slight too far away from the beach, or from a checkpoint, etc.
-Nanosuit is so Underpowered. The features are great and well thought out, but due to the double A batteries of the suit most of the abilities run out after about 5-10 seconds! Running is definetely the worst offender, because it is one of the most useful mechanics in the game (And would have made speedrunning quite easy!) it is just sapped away by the energy so quickly! This might not seem too important to some people, but remember if you are in a fire-fight with enemies and you just used a different Ability (eg.Cloak-Mode) your energy will be sapped and if you need to make a inhumanly-quick escape...you can see where this is going.
-Most of the Map is just jungle with beach attatched! it gets so boring after a little while and you always look for a car to drive quickly to the next location because you dont want to take a slow walk and "Enjoy" whats on offer. Because there really isnt much! although it may look very beautiful and all, it is not dense at all (Full with structures or unique features) much like Just Cause 1, 2 and 3! Although this is a linear shooter at the end of the day, it feels like in some sequences, its trying to awkwardly change that!
-Lots of Glitches (Obviously! no game is perfect..) that affect the game's graphics and also a crappy save system which, although being very manual to the player, has a very irritating habit of saving before a big battle. Now what would happen if you arrived early to said battle and were already taking lots of damage? Maybe an explosion happens at the last second? Save System: "Go Back 30 mins  to the slow-stealth section please!"
-Many minor parts of gameplay, controls or even visual effects will obviosuly be beaten by games today. So Ignorant players expecting a Battlefield 4 style Combat system will obviously not recieve it (The Combat/Weapon system and variety develops heavily in the second game!). Not really a Con, more of a "warning". But people know what they can expect now cant they!

Alright. Take a look at my hours. In this short amount of time, I can review this game with confidence.
I'd like to start off by saying that this is easily one of, if not THE best survival games I've ever played.
Now it's not a survival in the sense of minecraft, DAYZ, the forest, rust, etc.
In this case, survival means the most literal sense of the word, staying alive.  When a character dies, they are dead, and stay that way. A nice perma-death feature keeps you on your game.
You are trying to survive (and live...or continue living) in a war ravaged city. You need to hunt for food, medicine, things to keep you warm, weapons, and other survivors, well the ones that don't want to kill you...or raid your house while you're out...
This game does not hold your hand, it's gritty, it puts you in an environment, and into situations where you actually need to think about what to do with your short time with the cover of darkness. It tugs at your morals, and makes you think things you don't want to.
Is it worth going to the supermarket, knowing there are armed bandits, to get food because we are out? OR do we need to trade away our supplies for medicine, to save a woman and her children?
Every decision matters, try not to make bad ones....your game may end faster than it started.
BUT, you can always start over, make different decisions, kill (or help) more people, blah blah...
So with all that, I highly recommend this game if you are into any sort of survival, fight for your life game.

If you've played the first episode you know what you're in for.
If you haven't expect a zany, over the top, sometimes gross adventure game that makes just enough sense to be fun and coherent.
From a game design standpoint, everything is episode 2 is better than episode 1. The puzzles are more logical (and where they're not, the character's lines are so littered with clues that it will point you in the right direction just talking to people), the art is better, the voice acting is more consistent, the world is larger, Bertram is far more tolerable, the music is better and more diverse. Just a solid, well-designed adventure game.
On the downside, in its current form, the game is buggy as hell. From UI glitches, to audio issues (my music cut out halfway through the game and didn't come back until I closed out the game and reopened it, certain dialogue lines played twice), to misspelled subtitles (and not for comedic effect) to one outright gamebreaking bug. None of this was enough to ruin the experience, but it certainly colored it.
The only other modification I could think the game might need is a quest log. There was one point at which I accidentally skipped a line of dialogue... and then had no idea what I was supposed to be doing, regardless of the puzzle itself being pretty straightforward.
A fun little memorable jaunt and worthwhile experience.

There were a few game–stopping glitches early on, but after a week and a couple of quick updates, Rumpus Animation has pulled off a tremendously fun adventure game, poke-and-prod style.
The English accents, the witty puns with double–entenderings, and the crazy critters you have to deal with, make this little point-n-click adventure fun. It has a great musical score that changes with each scene, and the little sound effects and such are quite enjoyable to behold.

It's fun, it's entertaining, and it's a treat to listen to and watch as Bertram solves the case of the century. Or, well, maybe the conundrum of the afternoon. Whatever your cup of tea may be, this one will surely tickle your palate for an evening or two's enjoyment.
